# Plinth

> Plinth is a thin Go application kernel built on net/http. It owns typed HTTP binding, validation, RFC 9457 problems, OpenAPI, process lifecycle, and optional infrastructure adapters. Applications own business models and policy content.

## Start here

- [README](README.md): authoritative API and deployment reference.
- [Examples index](examples/README.md): documentation-only recipes plus runnable quickstart and deployment examples.
- [Runnable quickstart](examples/hello): dependency-free hello endpoint covered by `go test ./...`.
- [TLS and HTTP/2](examples/tls-http2): runnable in-process TLS/HTTP2 and reverse-proxy listener comparison.
- [Minimal HTTP](examples/minimal-http.md): typed endpoints and binding.
- [App shell](examples/app-shell.md): config, commands, logging, runtime.
- [JWT + Postgres authz](examples/jwt-postgres-authz.md): Bearer auth, DB permissions, route enforcement.
- [Declarative authz](examples/authz.md): permission tags and application policy sources.
- [CSRF](examples/csrf.md): cookie/header protection and bootstrap token.
- [CORS](examples/cors.md): explicit origin allowlist around the router.
- [Rate limits](examples/ratelimit.md): memory and Redis fixed-window middleware.
- [Sessions](examples/session.md): cookie-backed sessions and login/logout.
- [Security order](examples/security.md): middleware composition only.
- [Testing](examples/testing.md): testing application business logic with the real router.
- [Optional platform](examples/optional-platform.md): Postgres, Redis, database-neutral jobs/migrations with adapters, object storage.

## Notes for AI agents

- Framework types and public identifiers in examples are real; examples may omit imports.
- Unless a recipe demonstrates error handling, assume returned errors are nil and use `_`; keep code blocks near 15–35 lines.
- Do not add business domains or demo CRUD. Keep optional placeholder SQL minimal and clearly application-owned.
- Keep optional integrations out of core packages. Importing a core package must not link SCS, pgx, go-redis, Goose, JWT/OIDC, AWS, Prometheus, or OpenTelemetry.
- Use `router.Handle`/`Group.Handle` for typed HTTP. Use raw handlers only for streaming, upgrades, files, or explicit response control.
- Prefer the repository README and public API snapshot over the external `plinth-example` business application when deciding framework usage.
